basis:
Sizing calculations for the B'x layout-002 structure and lip: hand formulas with the trial loads.

    python -I -B structure_checks.py FIELD_TRIALS.json OUTPUT.json

Every row states its inputs, formula, value, allowable and margin (allowable / value, pass at >= 1.5 unless the row
says otherwise). Loads come from the field trials (rigid-lip, penalty-contact peaks, so they are upper estimates) and
from the stated abuse cases. Material allowables are handbook class values, not test data: polycarbonate yield
62 MPa and E 2.3 GPa, 6061-T6 yield 276 MPa, alloy-steel shaft yield 400 MPa and E 200 GPa, steel pin shear yield
230 MPa. Preliminary sizing only: no fatigue, no stress concentration, no fastener preload study.

rows.question: Does the sprung deployed stop hold the lip under the pipe standing on the tip?
rows.formula: moment about the hinge = M g a_tip + m_lip g a_tip / 2, against the stop preload

rows.question: How far does the 1/8 in polycarbonate lip sag under the pipe at the tip?
rows.formula: cantilever over the ramp: delta = M g / (3 EI / L^3)
rows.note: Allowable is a 3 mm drop of the 550 mm roll-off height; the 20 deg ramp trials (lower, slower) still capture

rows.question: Bending stress when the ejected pipe lands on the lip
rows.formula: energy into a cantilever: x = sqrt(2 E / k), F = k x, sigma = F a / (b t^2 / 6)

rows.question: Does the landing push the lip off its sprung stop far enough to change the roll-off?
rows.formula: worst case, all landing energy into the stop: theta = E / preload; tip drop = theta x tip radius
rows.note: Upper bound: the lip's own bending (L3) absorbs most of it first. 10 mm keeps the tip above the trough lip top (457.2 + 12 mm)

rows.question: Frontal hit on the lip tip (24.5 mm ahead of the bumper face): stress with the sprung stop yielding
rows.formula: the push acts 37.6 mm below the hinge and turns the lip down against the stop springs; sigma = F sin(30) L_ramp / (b t^2 / 6)

rows.question: Control: the same frontal travel on a rigid deployed stop (layout-001)
rows.formula: the ramp bends the whole travel: F = d k / sin^2(30); sigma = F sin(30) L / S
rows.note: Expected to fail: this is why the stop is sprung

rows.question: Hinge pins (two 3 mm steel pins, double shear) under the largest stop reaction plus the direct lip load
rows.formula: tau = (F_stop + F_lip) / (2 pins x 2 planes x A)

rows.question: Stop springs: preload each of two extension springs must carry at the 30 mm stop arm
rows.formula: F = preload / arm / 2
rows.note: Allowable is a catalogue-class limit for a 10 mm OD music-wire extension spring; select the article in detailed design

rows.question: Deploy swing: time from latch release to the deployed stop (torsion spring 0.10 N m plus gravity)
rows.formula: rigid lip about the hinge, I th'' = spring + m g r cos(angle), integrated from -120 deg
rows.note: The lip must be down before the first eject, about 10 s into TELEOP; arrival energy goes into the sprung stop

rows.question: Deploy arrival: over-travel of the sprung stop when the lip lands on it
rows.formula: theta = E / preload

rows.question: Bending stress in a 1/2 in steel hex roller shaft under the bite load spread along the pipe
rows.formula: simply supported, uniform load: M = F L / 8; sigma = M / (0.1203 d^3)

rows.question: Mid-span deflection of the steel hex shaft, against the 6 mm squeeze
rows.note: Allowable: a quarter of the squeeze. An aluminium shaft deflects 2.9 times as far, so the shafts are steel

rows.question: Bending stress in a 1/2 in steel hex roller shaft under the bite load spread along the pipe
rows.formula: simply supported, uniform load: M = F L / 8; sigma = M / (0.1203 d^3)

rows.question: Mid-span deflection of the steel hex shaft, against the 6 mm squeeze
rows.note: Allowable: a quarter of the squeeze. An aluminium shaft deflects 2.9 times as far, so the shafts are steel

rows.question: Bending stress in a 1/2 in steel hex roller shaft under the bite load spread along the pipe
rows.formula: simply supported, uniform load: M = F L / 8; sigma = M / (0.1203 d^3)

rows.question: Mid-span deflection of the steel hex shaft, against the 6 mm squeeze
rows.note: Allowable: a quarter of the squeeze. An aluminium shaft deflects 2.9 times as far, so the shafts are steel

rows.question: Side-plate landing: bolt tension from the receive impact (two 10-32 bolts per plate, 45 mm apart on the landing shelf)
rows.formula: horizontal F = 2 N (n_x + n_z mu) with tread mu 1.0; per plate T = (F / 2) h / s
rows.note: Allowable: 10-32 thread pull-out from 3 mm of 6061 (shear area pi d L / 2 at 200 MPa); the bolt itself proofs at 7.5 kN

rows.question: Pocket landing shelf: bending at the stringer edge with the P1 bolt tension applied at the side-plate line (1/4 in 6061, 200 mm long, 61.6 mm overhang)
rows.formula: sigma = 6 F a / (b t^2)
rows.note: The shelf carries the side-plate foot and the floor post inboard of the stringer, which has material only outboard of Y 232

rows.question: Pocket landing shelf: tip deflection under the same load
rows.formula: delta = F a^3 / (3 E I), I = b t^3 / 12, E = 69 GPa
rows.note: Allowable: 1 mm at the plate line

rows.question: Side-plate bending at the landing under the same impact (1/4 in 6061, 60 mm wide section, in plane)
rows.formula: sigma = M / (t w^2 / 6)

rows.question: Plate ligament between the two shaft bores under the band-maximum bite load (tension)
rows.formula: sigma = F / (2 plates x t x 40 mm)

rows.question: Gearbox static rating against the largest shaft torque in any trial (MAXPlanetary 1/2 in hex socket output)

inputs.source: REV MAXPlanetary load ratings: 3:1 stage tested to 290 N m, hex socket output fails at 250 N m

rows.formula: peak trial shaft torque against the weakest rated stage

rows.question: Drive torque at the 30 A limit against the mean torque that stalls it (the 240 N/mm bracket stalls; 160 passes)
rows.formula: T = Kt I N eta; the trials decide stall, this row records the number
rows.note: G2 measures the real efficiency: pass if the nip never stalls at 9 V on the installed tread
